fintech.headline: Indian fintechs grew in 2026 by changing products, licences and distribution routes rather than buying more traffic: AI in core operations, credit on UPI, cross-border payments and acquired distribution.

moves.move: Launched Vulcan, a payments AI foundation model, to improve payment success rates and detect international card fraud.
Launched Relay, AI agents that automate cart recovery, failed payment retries and COD confirmation for small businesses.
Launched P3P, a protocol that lets AI agents make UPI payments for users by extending UPI's mandate framework.
Launched Atlas, AI agents that run lender onboarding over WhatsApp, voice and video and assemble loan files.
Launched Kiwi Postpaid with YES Bank, a UPI credit line that needs no credit card.
Added Axis Bank as a third issuer for its co-branded travel credit card to approve more customers.
Launched Pye, a multi-lender platform giving retail borrowers access to many lenders through 1 interface.
Announced UAE operations as its first foreign market after in-principle approvals from the Central Bank of the UAE.
Launched cross-border payment acceptance for Indian exporters after RBI authorisation as a cross-border payment aggregator.
Gained GIFT City and RBI approvals for outward payments, turning export collections into a 2-way cross-border platform.
Launched card acceptance so Indian businesses can collect card payments from overseas buyers with INR payouts.
Acquired GreenLife Insurance Broking to enter insurance distribution for existing customers.
Announced plans to acquire credit marketplace IndiaLends, pending approval, to add a multi-lender user base.
Plans to scale Soundbox and EDC device sales and extend offline merchant acceptance beyond Tier I cities.

ecommerce.headline: Indian e-commerce growth in 2026 came from moving the store into AI assistants, selling internal infrastructure, going vertical in quick commerce and buying distribution.

moves.move: Let customers order food, groceries and dining reservations through AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini via MCP.
Launched Vaani, a Gen-AI voice shopping assistant for offline-first shoppers.
Made Nykaa Beauty and Nykaa Fashion connected apps inside ChatGPT, routing purchases to Nykaa's own app or site.
Launched a multi-brand D2C shopping experience inside ChatGPT with PayU, from discovery to payment.
Opened its pan-India logistics network and warehousing to MSMEs, D2C brands and enterprises.
Began selling Delhivery Maps, its internally built AI geospatial APIs, to external enterprises and developers.
Launched Shipsy Brain in beta, an AI layer that lets agents make and execute logistics decisions on live orders.
Expanded its quality-first grocery model to citywide coverage across Bengaluru, competing on trust rather than speed.
Extended fashion quick commerce into jewellery, handbags, footwear and beauty.
Launched Mall-to-Home delivery from partner fashion stores in Mumbai in about 120 minutes without holding stock.
Added 30-minute pet care delivery from partner-operated dark stores and clinics.
Launched 10-minute food delivery in Gurugram, its first major expansion beyond Karnataka.
Agreed to acquire Swiggy's LYNK retail distribution business in a share swap.
Acquired Zodiac Labs AI to add quick commerce analytics and purchase tools for D2C brands.

healthtech.headline: Indian healthtech companies grew in 2026 by owning more of the patient journey; 7 of 13 moves were acquisitions or mergers.

moves.move: Reopened US pre-orders for a redesigned ring assembled in Texas after an import restriction.
Agreed to acquire Singapore oral care brand Zenyum, extending its aligner business across 10 countries.
Agreed to acquire London longevity medicine practice Longevous.
Merged with US virtual nutrition provider Berry Street to reach patients through insurance-covered care.
Opened its own hospitals in Delhi-NCR with insurance approvals handled before admission.
Acquired Superclaims, an AI claims platform, to sell claims processing to insurers and TPAs.
Expanding a physical omnichannel store network, aiming for about 500 stores by end-2026.
Acquired Pune-based Megavision Diagnostics, entering radiology beyond pathology.
Agreed to buy Guwahati diagnostic centre Arya Wellness, entering North-East India.
Acquired Saveo Healthtech's pharmacy distribution business serving pharmacies across South India.
Launched a prepaid annual diagnostics plan replacing pay-per-test pricing.
Launched Parrotlet-a v2, a clinical speech model for Hindi and Indian English, opened through developer APIs.
Launched Nightingale, a hospital video foundation model, and began expanding into the US.

saas.headline: Indian SaaS growth in 2026 came from products that execute work rather than track it, bought capability, and new surfaces and markets.

moves.move: Launched a single conversational AI interface across its apps and entered vertical SaaS with 7 industry applications.
Repositioned around employee experience and added a no-code AI agent studio priced per session.
Rebuilt its HCM platform as AI-native with Cortex and took it to the US market.
Launched Nitro, agents that complete billable professional services tasks inside project workflows.
Launched autonomous compliance agents, then opened an Australian data centre.
Made its AI Workforce Platform generally available, selling governed AI coworkers with defined roles and permissions.
Packaged pre-trained AI employees into HR, IT and Finance hubs.
Launched facilities management agents that run on existing CMMS, ERP and finance systems.
Acquired Fern to extend into API documentation and SDK generation.
Acquired Aampe to add per-user AI decisioning above its campaign tools.
Acquired UK-based Seldon AI to move its machine learning customers onto TrueFoundry's AI Gateway.
Acquired Verloop.io to add chat automation to its voice AI platform, then rebranded.
Launched a mobile app that turns a spoken idea into a working app published to app stores.
Took its Harmony agentic CX platform to the UAE and Saudi Arabia.
